input: Draft a five-year career progression roadmap

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's current role, seniority level, and industry defines the realistic starting point and what 'progression' actually means for them — a junior developer's roadmap looks nothing like a mid-level marketing manager's.
Whether this roadmap is for the user alone, to share with a manager, or to present in a performance review changes the tone, depth, and level of professional framing required.
The destination — a specific title, salary band, skill set, or lifestyle — is the single biggest driver of what milestones to include and how ambitious to make each step.
Whether the user plans to stay at their current employer, move companies, go freelance, or start a business entirely changes which actions and timelines are realistic.
Hard limits like time available for learning, geographic restrictions, financial obligations, or caregiving responsibilities directly cap which paths are feasible.

Some people want a highly structured, month-by-month breakdown; others want broad annual themes. The level of granularity and emphasis (skills vs. titles vs. income vs. work-life balance) shapes the whole format.
The intended output format — a written narrative, a table, a slide deck, a visual timeline — determines how the content should be structured and delivered.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a five-year career progression roadmap
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured, personalised plan that maps out the user's career growth, milestones, and actions over the next five years.

questions.title: What is your current role, level, and industry?
questions.description: Establish the user's starting point — job title, seniority, and the field they work in — so the roadmap begins from a realistic baseline.

questions.title: Who will read or use this roadmap?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a private personal plan, something to share with a manager, or a document for a formal review process, which affects tone and framing.

questions.title: What does career success look like for you in five years?
questions.description: Identify the user's target destination — whether that is a specific title, income level, skill mastery, leadership role, or a different definition of success.

questions.title: Do you plan to stay at your current employer or move on?
questions.description: Clarify whether the roadmap should be built around internal promotion paths, job-hopping, freelancing, entrepreneurship, or a combination.

questions.title: What is your biggest constraint — time, money, location, or other?
questions.description: Surface the hardest limits that will cap certain paths, such as limited study time, financial obligations, geographic immobility, or caregiving responsibilities.

questions.title: Should the roadmap focus more on skills, titles, income, or balance?
questions.description: Understand the user's priorities so the milestones emphasise what matters most to them rather than a generic one-size-fits-all career ladder.

questions.title: What format do you want the final roadmap delivered in?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a written narrative, a structured table, a visual timeline, a slide deck, or another format for the output.
